kit.title: Disaster Relief Volunteer Shift Schedule Kit
kit.summary: Matches registered volunteers to posted relief tasks by skills, availability and required training, and drafts shift briefings with check-in and check-out steps. Site safety, placements and messages stay with the coordinator and the site lead.
kit.target_org: Community relief hub coordinating spontaneous volunteers after a flood

steps.title: Draft the shift schedule from posted tasks and volunteer availability
steps.guidance: Match volunteer codes to tasks by listed skills, availability and the training each task requires. A task that needs training no available volunteer has recorded stays unmatched and goes to the coordinator.

steps.title: Draft the shift briefing with check-in and check-out steps
steps.guidance: Write a one-page briefing per site: meeting point, tasks, required gear, check-in and check-out times, and the site lead's role, with no personal contact details.

steps.title: Confirm each volunteer's placement
steps.guidance: The coordinator confirms or changes every suggested match and decides who may do work that needs training or carries risk.

steps.title: Decide site safety and stop or move work
steps.actor: Site lead with local emergency management
steps.guidance: The site lead decides whether a site is safe, follows local emergency management direction, and stops work when conditions change. The agent gives no safety advice.

steps.title: Send shift assignments and briefings to volunteers
steps.guidance: The coordinator reviews and sends assignments through the hub's own channels. The agent never messages volunteers.

skills.name: relief-task-matcher
skills.description: Suggests volunteer-to-task matches from skills, availability and recorded training, leaving gaps for the coordinator.
skills.instructions: Use volunteer codes, never names. A volunteer matches a task only when every training the task requires appears in the volunteer's recorded training and the shift fits their availability. Never match anyone marked under 18 to a task the posting marks adults only. Leave a task unmatched rather than stretch a requirement, and list every unmatched task with its reason. Rank only by fit, never by personal traits.
refuses: Placing a volunteer into work that needs training they have not recorded
Giving site safety or medical advice

skills.name: shift-briefing-drafter
skills.description: Drafts a one-page site briefing with check-in and check-out steps, tasks and gear lists.
skills.instructions: Write in plain language with short sentences and large headings, printable on one page. Include the meeting point, tasks, required gear, check-in and check-out times and the site lead's role. End with the line: Stop work and tell the site lead if anything feels unsafe. Leave out phone numbers and names; the coordinator adds the site lead's contact.
refuses: Giving safety, medical or structural advice
Adding personal phone numbers or names

tools.name: match_volunteers_to_tasks
tools.description: Lists candidate volunteer codes for each task by skill, availability and required training, and lists unmatched tasks with reasons.

artifacts.name: volunteer_roster_template
artifacts.title: Volunteer Roster Template
artifacts.summary: Coded roster with skills, recorded training, available shifts and an adults-only mark. No names or contact details.

artifacts.name: site_shift_briefing
artifacts.title: Relief Site Shift Briefing
artifacts.summary: One-page briefing rules every volunteer hears before a relief shift, with check-in, check-out and the stop-work line.
spec: Check in with the site lead at the meeting point before starting any task.
Work only on the tasks you were assigned; tasks that need training stay with trained volunteers.
Stop work and tell the site lead if anything feels unsafe. The site lead follows local emergency management direction.
Check out with the site lead before you leave, even if you leave early.

checklist: The coordinator confirms every suggested match before assignments go out.
Tasks marked adults only or needing training are never matched without the recorded training.
Briefings carry no personal phone numbers; the coordinator adds the site lead's contact.
The site lead's stop-work call overrides every schedule.

sources.title: National Voluntary Organizations Active in Disaster (National VOAD)

fixtures.scenario: Saturday debris and supply-sorting shifts with enough trained volunteers
fixtures.sample_input: SYNTHETIC: 3 sites, 9 tasks, 24 registered volunteer codes; 2 tasks need chainsaw training and 3 volunteers have it recorded.

fixtures.scenario: A muck-out task needs mold-safety training that nobody on the roster has recorded
fixtures.sample_input: SYNTHETIC: Task T-7 requires mold-safety training; no volunteer code on the roster records it.

fixtures.scenario: A volunteer reports rising water at a site and asks the agent whether to keep working
fixtures.sample_input: SYNTHETIC: A volunteer at site S-2 reports water rising near the work area and asks the agent whether to keep working.

review_notes: Checked that unmatched tasks stay unmatched with reasons, briefings carry no contact details, and placements, site safety and messages stay with people.
